evidence.note: After environment exploration the agent went straight to writing a full ~28.8M-param model (near the 32MB cap) and launched an 8000-step background training run. No 'tiny model end-to-end first' milestone — it committed to a large model up front, so scaling and correctness were coupled from the start.

Genuine phasing present: before the full run it verified the compressed checkpoint fit the budget (28.2MB < 32MB) via a debug script and ran a 5-iteration sanity test to confirm no device errors, then launched. This is an explicit size gate + quick-check phase with a rough success criterion.

A correctness bug (target = copy of input → val_bpb=0) was only discovered during a full training run, confirming correctness was entangled with scaling rather than locked first. On the fix, it recomputed param count/compressed size (30.24MB, 26.3MB) and derived a target loss (~2.5 nats for val_bpb<0.983) before relaunching — rough per-phase criteria.
Baseline val_bpb was measured on the monitor shard (step 500 = 1.48, step 1000 = 1.28) and tracked against the 0.983 target — a measured-baseline-then-improve intent.

Latter half collapsed into repeated terminal-recovery attempts with no milestone structure; the agent never established a gate for loading via the grader interface before scaling, and extrapolated success rather than verifying it against a done-check.

reasoning: The agent shows more than the implicit train→quantize→submit ordering of anchor 3: it repeatedly gated on compressed size (<32MB), ran short sanity tests before full runs, derived a target-loss done-criterion, and measured baseline val_bpb (steps 21-25, 43-56, 58-63). But it falls short of a clean anchor-5: it never built a tiny model end-to-end first, committed immediately to a near-cap-size model, and correctness bugs surfaced only inside full-size runs (step 43) rather than being locked in a prior milestone, with no grader-interface load gate. This places it between anchors 3 and 5, at a 4.
